From: Ron Smith, WATFORD

It's great to receive the latest
OUTLET 46! My how time flies!
The disc lives up to its usual
standard which is excellent -
the work you must put in not
only for SAM but all the others!
May the SAM always shine upon
you all.

Now the query: have you the
answer for transferring PCG's
DESK TOP PUBLISHER to SAM via
LERM's SAM SPEC? I've tried all
ways but with no success .

I have WORDMASTER on disc so
first I have to transfer it to
tape. The answer LERM gave is as
follows...

1 MERGE d1 "WORD" 2 SAVE TO TAPE
by "SAVE "WORD" LINE 10 ENTER
CLEAR 54173.LOAD *"m";1;"WM"CODE
(my instructions do not mention
CODE on the end but it will not
LOAD without it) SAVE to tape so
SAVE "WM"CODE 54174,11362.

After loading SAMSPEC and then
SPEC from LERM's disc you then
load in WORDMASTER from the tape
with LOAD "". What happens? -
Nothing! After loading the BASIC
"WORD" from tape, the screen is
clear - no more lines - nothing.
The code has vanished although
it was on the tape. Verifying
confirmed it was there. Now I
know it does transfer as many
have already succeeded. Can you
please tell me why I cannot do
it?

I wrote to LERM but they never
answered my letter even though I
am a member of SAM's SOFTWARE
CLUB. Keep up the good work and
I hope that many SAM programs
using all its potential will be
with us - not just SPECTRUM
conversions. Happy computing.

            Regards,

            Ron Smith

Brian Cavers to Ron Smith

After you MERGE"WORD",enter LIST
and look for the line that loads
the code from disc. This will
be something like...

   LOAD*"m";1;"WM"CODE or...

   LOAD d1;"WM"CODE

Alter this line to LOAD "WM"CODE
and then proceed to SAVE it to
tape as you did before. You see,
I think the BASIC was loading
from tape into SAM but then it
was trying to use Microdrive or
+D/Disciple syntax to load the
code from disc instead of load-
ing it from tape. Let me know
how you get on.
                   - Brian

 From George Robson
Your readers might be interested
to know the Sam MESSENGER in its
present form will not fit on the
edge connector of a Spectrum +3
because the PSU input lead is in
the way. To fit, it has to be
taken out of its case. Also for
the +3, two of the pins standing
up near the edge-connector of
the MESSENGER have to be joined.
These points were passed on by
Bruce Gordon. I cannot say if it
then works or not as I returned
my MESSENGER to SAMCO as I was
unable to get it working. I am
awaiting a report on it at pres-
ent but one wonders if there are
more problems caused by the +3.
              - George Robson

Thanks. Keep us updated! - BRIAN

From Darrell Ottery, SOMERSET

Many thanks for the latest OUT-
LET.The new colourful layout for
the Sam is a great improvement.
Who's the artist?

Can a Tasword +2 file (Opentype)
be converted to Tasword 2 (or
Outwrite)format?The reason being
I have several files I wish to
transfer and I don't really want
to retype them all.

Many thanks for sorting out my
problems with Masterdos.I had,in
fact,typed the letter correctly.
I appear to have misread the
manual. I'm sure it indicated by
pressing 'a' after a named file
copy would copy all subsequent
files. Never mind.

I'd also like to thank you for
your help with the Drivechat
article in Issue 42. I've been
in touch with Malcolm Perry and,
though unfortunately he'd sold
his set-up by the time I wrote
to him, he has since built me a
similar system which is perfect
for my needs. I'd like to thank
him through Outlet if I may for
all his help and time.

I'm thinking about getting Music
Writer, especially having just
read about the extension program
to allow music to be played back
independently. Is it possible to
convert it for +D use. I know it
could be snapped easily enough
but can it be converted to load
and save from disc?

I've just sent off for Domark's
3D Construction Kit. Once it
arrives would you like a review?

I'm typing this on Outwrite! as
you'll probably see from the
code start on the disc. It is
truly excellent, by far the best
WP package I've used and I'm
sure in forthcoming issues will
continue to be improved (if that
is possible). A Search/Replace
routine would be nice at some
stage.

At last I've a piece of software
with which I feel comfortable
when typing. The instruction
manual is very good and at the
moment I don't seem to have any
queries or problems.

One question that has just
occured to me,so ignore the last
line, is why the multitude of
fonts?There are perhaps only one
or two as legible as the
standard one. The only reason I
could think of was perhaps for
designing screen$ (a very useful
feature) but being limited to
only 1 font per file, mixing
fonts appears impossible.

Have any of your readers bought
any copies of Enceladus? I think
it is fantastic,including useful
unprotected programs, demos,
stunning presentation(especially
the latest issue, No. 5) and a
fairly light-hearted editorial.
Graham Burtenshaw is to be
congratulated on doing such a
fine job.

For those of you who haven't got
a copy yet,do so immediately.The
best way to describe it is by
comparison to the high quality
of Outlet with the wit of Your
Sinclair of late. With 4 quality
magazines already (Outlet,
Enceladus, Sam Supplement and
Fred) the Coupe will soon be
bettering the 16-bits.

Glad to hear the mouse is out at
long last.I intend to buy one at
the show.Price `40 or `50 if you
want a trackerball instead but I
did hear the interface will sell
for `30 without the mouse, being
a standard so any serial mouse
will work,e.g.,an ST-compatible
mouse which can be bought fairly
cheaply for a good rodent.

What's this I hear about a hard
drive? Apparently a 40Mb hard
drive will become available that
fits inside one of the internal
drive slots.Does anyone know any
more?

I'll sign off for now with just
a note about GM_Calc which I
also got recently. Very good for
my needs(tabulating data etc)but
a bit slow on the calculation
front (but that's because of
BASIC). I'd like to see a MC
version that could be bigger for
an expanded machine.

Best of luck with the house
moving.
             Yours,

         Darrell Ottery

Brian Cavers to Darrell Ottery

Thanks, Darrell. I'm the one who
drew the new CONTENTS page. The
graphics in our text mode are PD
screens I converted to Mode 3
and coloured and modified.

Glad you're happy with OUTWRITE!
The fonts were added to give
users a choice as different
people have different tastes. It
may be that others will prefer
ones you don't!In any event it's
far better to have too many than
only one and NO choice, right?

Yes, it is possible to convert
open-type files to OUTWRITE-type
format using "T3TO2" in the next
issue of OUTLET.

I've often wondered before how
Tasword +2 can use open-type
files. I mean, the +2 is a tape-
based machine and there is no
standard disc drive so what is
meant by "open-type" in Tasword
+2? Surely they cannot be on
tape? It doesn't make sense. I'm
extremely curious about this!Let
me know.

Incidentally, "T3TO2" is a new
SAM/Disciple/+D version of a Tas
3 to 2 convertor. You must have
MASTERDOS booted to use it on
SAM. If your files are on +D or
Disciple disc they load in T3TO2
on SAM or +D for conversion.

I'll put your SPECMAKER review
in a future issue.

Regrettably, MUSIC WRITER cannot
cope with other systems but is
dedicated to tape or +3 disc. It
is a shame but much software is
limited to a smaller market just
because it accesses the media
direct from machine code. It is
much easier to return to BASIC
to SAVE and LOAD and the program
is then more easily-modifiable.
We get lots and lots of requests
asking how to convert programs
to other systems. Software prod-
ucers just don't seem to know
that they are missing increased
sales.

Yes, yes - please do a review of
3D Construction kit. If you can
snap 2 or 3 screen shots too it
would be great!

As for Enceladus I shall order a
copy soon.No doubt we shall lose
a few customers because of your
letter but hopefully you'll
do the decent thing and write to
Enceladus to tell THEIR readers
how good OUTLET is?

The latest on the mouse appears
to be that the interface WON'T
be sold separately from the
mouse - at least, that's the way
the latest SAMCO newsletter
reads.

I know nothing more about the
hard drive  other than rumour.I,
for one, would be interested in
getting one if and when it was
available although I suspect it
is just speculation at present.

We should have a review of GM_
CALC soon. However, as mentioned
previously, we are negotiating a
deal to produce a new machine
code spreadsheet that Ron says
is far better than anything yet
seen on Spectrum or SAM. At the
moment it is a Spectrum program
but the author hopes to do a SAM
version. In addition, there is a
wordprocessor/database/spread-
sheet package being developed by
DANSOFT for an autumn launch so
watch this space...

                       - Brian

From Derek Burn

Dear Editors,

This letter is being prepared
using a Coupe adaptation of
Tasword Two. This has been,until
recently, the only really
viable way of word processing on
the Coupe but I, like I'm sure
many other Coupe owners, have
been impatiently awaiting a
definitive word processor for
our excellent machines.

I was therefore delighted to
learn about your OUTWRITE and
have now gained some experience
with it. I would sum it up as a
fairly competent implementation
of a Tasword Two look-alike.

It's major advantage is, of
course, that it is designed for
the Coupe, thus avoiding the
need to refer back to the
Spectrum from time to time; it
also takes advantage of some of
the features of the Coupe not
present on the Spectrum.

Having said that, is it a suffi-
ciently professional and worthy
product for the Coupe? Does it
significantly advance the art of
word processing on the Coupe? I
think not.

Before acquiring a Coupe I had
been using a Spectrum Plus Two/
Disciple set-up with Tasword
Plus Two. By taking full
advantage of the extra memory

available with the Plus Two (and
also with the Spectrum Plus
Three), Tasman had produced a
product which is streets ahead
of Tasword Two and one which can
claim to be a truly professional
tool. Even if one does not wish
to use some of its more advanced
capabilities, surely no current
word processor can afford to be
without them. Indeed, I would
maintain that Tasword Plus Two
represents the minimum accept-
able standard for a machine as
advanced as the Coupe.

Given that the basic Coupe has
256K of memory, we should,
therefore, be entitled to expect
a product offering at least
equivalent features to Tasword

Plus Two (or Tasword Plus Three)
and probably much more as well.
Indeed, a product comparable to
Tasword PC is not asking too
much, particularly if one con-
siders the 500K that many owners
are likely to have available.

Given their proven expertise and
professionalism, I'm sure Tasman
are the best-qualified people to
produce such a piece of soft-
ware. Unfortunately, when I last
spoke to them, they appeared to
be somewhat disinterested.Surely
it is about time they recognised
that the Coupe is here to stay,
that it is going from strength
to strength and that it is
crying out for a word processor
worthy of it?
                   - Derek Burn

Brian Cavers to Derek Burn

Much of what you say is true and
I understand the spirit of dis-
appointment in which your letter
is written. However, I must dis-
agree with some of your state-
ments.

No software has any obligation
to be "worthy" of a machine or
to "advance the art". OUTWRITE
is what it claims to be and we
never use any hype to make it
seems to be more.It is a budget-
priced product and does not need
to justify its existence because
it does not meet the needs of
everyone.Most OUTWRITE users are
delighted with it(see the letter
before this one).

At least one other wordprocessor
is being developed for SAM and
is likely to be more advanced in
its features but I, for one,
would be extremely annoyed if I
only had the choice of one word
processor on my machine and that
choice was to pay `50 plus for
features I would never use like
mail-merge, auto-page numbering,
headers and footers, rulers,
spell-checkers and so on and on
and on. Most home-users wouldn't
know what to do with a mail-
merge facility if it bit them on
the nose.We run a small business
but find it more efficient to
do mass mail-shots by having the
letter commercially printed or
photocopied and using label
addresses rather than printing
every single letter.

You say that Tasword +2 and +3
are streets ahead of Tasword 2.
I,myself, have most Taswords yet
I, like many others, am happy
with the simplicity of Tasword 2
- please believe me,USERS DO NOT
NECESSARILY WANT MOST OF THE
ADVANCED FEATURES THAT YOU WANT.

The implication of your letter
when you say "no current word
processor can afford to be with-
out[more advanced capabilities]"
when taken to another market
would be that the popular cars
should not be available but only
Rolls-Royces. I think you go too
far when you say "Tasword Plus
Two represents the minimum
acceptable standard" - shall the
rest of us all conform to what
is acceptable to you?

I cannot understand why you want
to have a "minimum standard". It
seems to me there is room for
all - high and low, modest, good
and brilliant.

Shall we sweep OUTWRITE under
the carpet if something more
advanced comes along at `99.99
because it does not have the
same features? I think not. The
entire answer to your letter is
in the price. OUTWRITE is only
`12 to OUTLET readers. If Tasman
invested the many thousands of
pounds needed over many, many
months to develop an advanced
word processor for the SAM, do
your really think it would sell
for less than `30? It might be a
lot lot more!

I accept that you know that the
SAM is capable of much more and
you WANT more out of a word
processor than is available at
present but "live and let live",
say I. Let's not draw any chalk
marks or impose any standards
for everyone because we want a
certain specification for
ourselves.

Finally, faced with disappoint-
ment, I must say, the world does
not owe us ANYTHING; we are not
"entitled" to ANYTHING and no
company has any DUTY to produce
what we want.

Sorry If I sounded harsh but I
felt I must put my point of view
on this.
                        - Brian

From: G.A. Matthews, BARKING

Re: the bit about Specmaker in
OUTLET, I have this program.It's
like the curate's egg - good in
parts. It is  less easy to use
than Lerm's tape (by the way, do
you know Lerm Tape 4 is heavily
protected, that is, you cannot
easily copy it -you have to have
the master disk or it won't
work).

Specmaker does not (or I cannot
get it to) work with Tasword or
Mini Office. It does work with
Wordmaster/Headliner/Typeliner,
Art Studio 48K and Graphics
Creator.I wouldn't bother to try
it with games. The instructions
give details of how to transfer

the Plus D version of OUTLET to
SAM using Specmaker. Specmaker
does have the advantage of being
able to have a lot of small
programs in RAM disk -ideal with
P.C.G.'s DTP.

I have come to the conclusion
that there are several versions
of SAMDOS which interact with
some programs. I had a lot of
problems with some programs
which were cured when I tried
them again with a later version
of SAMDOS. This also applies to
Masterdos. I bought an early
version which insisted that I
had only one drive. Talking to a
friend, he said he had no prob-
lems with it. I got him to let
me have a copy of his version -
problem cured.

Either he had a later version
(his is called MDOS 31, mine
MDOS 2) or mine was a rogue
version.

I also think there are several
versions of Tasword 2,with minor
differences.
             - G.A. Matthews



You've not been reading OUTLET
carefully as these differences
have been mentioned before! The
drive 2 problem is cured with a
POKE as I recollect. I sometimes
find my drive 2 cannot be used
and it's because I have booted a
reader's disc with a dos set up
for ONE drive!       - Brian.

From Jim Hossack, WEST KILBRIDE



Dear Brian,

When I switch on my +3, all
memory locations above 24000 or
thereabouts are zero, except for
40122. This shows 127. Wonder if
this is a normal bug in a +3 or
if it's just in my particular
one? Although I've had the setup
for 2 years, I never noticed it
before. Then I used a machine
code routine to check memory
downwards for the first blank
space and it showed up. Could it
have been hiding there all the
time, I wonder?

Is there a Copier program to let
me load a tape program into the
+3 then unload it to disk(I have
a LERM copier which does this
tape - 2nd tape). At the moment,
I can usually "fiddle" a tape on
to disk but a program would make
life easier.


Finally, I've never been able to
get Tasword to print of its own
accord (Panasonic KP 1081)but by
adding the routine from your
Outclass, part 2(Issue 13) where
you refer to 8232 in ROM,I have
got it to print - see lines 1200
to 1250 in the program. I just
wonder why it doesn't print by
itself; presumably the +2 and +3
need the same m/c lines?

After learning a bit about
machine code, a year or so ago I
adapted my radio call-sign/log
book search, at that time in
very slow BASIC, to machine code
as follows:


Search for first char. of call-
sign, if found set register bit
0, then 2nd char., set bit 1 and
so on to bit 5 and the full 6
chars then compare the resulting
register with 63, put into
accumulator, if all bits set, =
63, unload HL,nn, peek nn and
take it from there.

So far so good, and all worked
fine and still does with this
program.

I had 32 memory locations
reserved for each call-sign - 6
for the call chars. themselves,
and 26 for date, remarks, etc.
So after each full search loop,
I incremented the HL register by
27 (ADC 27), having already inc.
it 5 times - once between each
call char. - during the search,
giving 32 total.

A few weeks ago, I decided to
use the same search program with
"COMPASS" [in a future OUTLET]
increasing the search chars. to
8, but reducing the memory bank
from 32 to 20, as I only needed
"town" & "co-ords".

So, again I incremented HL
between letters, now 7 times

instead of 5, plus ADC 13, with
rel. jump adjustments. Again,
apparently, 100 per cent OK.

Unfortunately, it only worked
for the first dozen or so town
names, then stopped (I had set
BC to do 920 circuits, so why
only 12?).

After much hair-tearing and
nail-biting in the region of BC,
I decided to have a good look at
the program with your disassemb-
ler. (Extra No.1).

Apparently all was O.K. then on
the third perusal I got it.
Instead of incrementing HL
between letters, (23 H), as I
intended to do, I had used 2C H

(inc L), which was fine for 5 +
ADC 27. With inc 7 times + ADC
13. However, one inc L was
falling just where the register
changed over, 255-256 (work it
out!) giving 255-0 instead.

This is probably a good example
of a potential bug in a program
which doesn't show until you try
to alter it, even ever so
slightly!Moral -always make sure
you use the exact instruction
you want!
                 - Jim Hossack

Eh? What? Oh, yes, certainly. I
agree. Yes, I get 127 in 40122
too so it's a +3 bug. I'd heard
it corrupts one or two addresses
after NEW as well.     - Brian

From Martin Tomes,

I have a CITIZEN 120+D printer
which is excellent to work with
as the manual is very easy to
follow except for the download-
ing of fonts. I can redefine the
standard 120+ font but is it
possible to load in one of the
OUTWRITE fonts or SAM's to get a
printout of that font?.

ESC;"-20": = OFF. [The hyphen in

DEC,27,254,50,49 & 27,254,50,48

How about an article on how to
get the most from a printer? I
realise printers vary a lot from
one to another but the basic
ideas would be a help - like
entering the codes correctly.

I cannot get the program OUTDEX
to run. I get an error message
29 (310:1, 440:1, 540:1). The
only lines I can find something
wrong with are 330, 480,540.
which all read the same as shown
on the next page...

330 PRINT #S;" ";N$;".......
..........................." (TO
26-LEN N$);I$;" " ;C$(C);L$

I get dumps from FLASH with no
trouble at all.

         - Martin Tomes

Brian Cavers to Martin Tomes

You say you"find something wrong
with... lines 330, 480, 540" but
you don't say WHAT is wrong with
them. As I remember, they work
correctly but if you try to edit
the line in BASIC the syntax
checker won't let you re-enter
the line! This is because it
assumes the brackets must only
be used with a string variable
and not a string constant.

That's just a red herring. The
real problem I suspect is with
the READ statement and the old
BASIC page boundary problems. It
may be you have an old ROM SAM.
Please enter PRINT PEEK 15 and
let me know the value shown.

You might also try entering...

1 DIM BUG$(5000)
                 ...then run it.

This sometimes clears the bug
but will be awkward with OUTDEX
which is updated each month.

Please send me a copy of your
OUTDEX for me to check. Use the
COPY command to put it on a
spare disc (which I'll return)
thus...

    COPY "OUTDEX" TO "OUTDEX"

            ...but DON'T do this
in Mode 1 as it doesn't work.

I've got a bad feeling about
this bug...

I have a copy of part of the
Citizen 120D manual but not the
part about down-loading fonts.
However, I'm pretty sure that it
uses a different font design
that would be calculated up and
down whereas screen fonts are
left and right. Has anyone else
worked out how to download fonts
to the 120D? We did have an
article about down-loading fonts
some time ago but I think it was
for the LC10 printer.If all else
fails then send me a photocopy
of the relevant pages of the
120D manual about down-loading
fonts. A BASIC routine ought to
be able to convert the fonts.

I'd warmly welcome articles on
printers as suggested.
                        - Brian

From L.J. Hall, BOURNEMOUTH

Can you please explain how to
transfer the MASTERFILE files
from my OUTLET 45 on +D disc to
a 3", +3 disc in 128K mode?
QQ
Via tape if you have a recorder.
Type this in...

10 FOR N=2 TO 9
20 LOAD d1"std"+STR$ N DATA F$()
30 SAVE   "std"+STR$ N DATA F$()
40 NEXT N

Same on the +3 but remove the d1
in line 20 and add: 5 LOAD "T:"

Wait a good few seconds between
saves so the +3 has time to save
to disc between loads.  - Brian.

From Darrell Ottery, SOMERSET
